A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same distribution-prompting study. The main text, equations, all 13 figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and can be matched despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original prompt-tuning experiments in Sections 5.1–5.4, a prefix-length ablation in Appendix B, and POS-specific experiments comparing base and instruction-tuned models in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including approximation-loss measurements, distribution-shuffling and cross-model experiments, and the appendix ablation and POS case study.

M1.justification: Target construction and hard, soft, and hybrid prompt tuning remain unchanged, including objectives and updates in Equations (1)–(5). Added explanations of frozen parameters and soft-prompt scope do not modify the procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate entropy-controlled, outlier, LM-generated, shuffled, cross-model, and POS-specific target distributions. Appendix C already contains the POS and instruction-tuned-model coverage in v1.

E2.justification: The comparison sets are retained: hard/soft/hybrid prompting, pretrained versus randomly initialized models, and base versus instruction-tuned Llama and Qwen models. No comparator is added or removed from these experiments.

E3.justification: The KL-divergence metric and experimental settings are unchanged. Both retain the 0.05 entropy step and Appendix B's default prefix length of 5, learning rate of 0.1, 500-epoch maximum, and 20-epoch early-stopping patience.

E4.justification: The random-weight comparison, outlier analysis, token-shuffling tests, prefix-length ablation, and POS/instruction-tuning case study are retained. Rewritten explanations and relocated appendix figures introduce no additional analysis.

E5.justification: Initialization counts and aggregation practices remain unchanged, including five initializations in the standard setup and 25 per target in Section 5.3. Figure 1's standard-error bands and Figures 5 and 7's 95% confidence intervals are retained.

E6.justification: The plotted results and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Figure 8a retains R² values of 0.018 for LM-generated targets and 0.801 for constructed targets. No result entries are added or removed, including in the appendices.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and Appendix A's entropy and outlier-mass derivations are unchanged. Section 3 clarifies token-index notation from Z_+ to Z_≥0, while Section 4.1 adds intuition for Equation (2); neither changes the underlying mathematical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract's three central findings and the claimed contribution of probing LM expressivity through distribution prompting are retained. The revised introduction and conclusion do not introduce a new demonstrated contribution.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly frames soft prompts as probing theoretical reachability despite potentially leaving the natural input manifold. Section 6 adds possible applications to prompt design, distribution-aware decoding, failure detection, and model evaluation. Existing mechanistic hypotheses and limitations remain.

D1.justification: Optimization details, initialization procedures, and Appendix C's ScispaCy tagging and token-filtering instructions are retained. V2 adds no substantive implementation, hardware, runtime, or code/data-access information.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work positioning are unchanged, including the relationships to softmax bottlenecks, prior prompt-tuning methods, and LM-output inversion.

P1.justification: V2 adds explanatory passages in the introduction and methods, tightens several experimental and concluding paragraphs, and corrects wording. It also adds an author-affiliation footnote and acknowledgements. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All 13 figures retain their plotted content and numbering. Figures 3 and 11 move between columns, Figure 13 moves to the final page, and text reflows around the retained figures. This is a limited layout revision.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies the purpose and applicability of unconstrained soft prompts, explains the outlier-mass constraint more accessibly, and improves several experimental and discussion paragraphs. These changes modestly improve readability and scope transparency. The experiments, results, and derivations remain unchanged, so the improvement is explanatory rather than a substantial strengthening of the evidence.
